Enable customers:read for the connection check, plus the read scopes for resources you use and customers:write, items:write, jobs:write or events:write for your writes. The full key is shown only once.

UrableCreateJobConfig.description: Create a job. Requires scope `jobs:write`. Send line items as product/service references + quantities; the server looks up prices, embeds the products, and computes the invoice subtotal/tax/total. A sequential `num` is assigned. Requires a customer, an `industry`, at least one `itemId`, and at least one line item. A job's work is always tracked per item, so the invoice comes back with the line items grouped under `invoice.items` — keyed by item ref — rather than as a flat `invoice.lineItems` array. On a job with one item every line item belongs to it; on a job with several, each line item must name its `itemId`, and every item needs at least one line item. A `field` job is performed on site, so it also needs a `location`: send one, or omit it and the customer's location is copied onto the job. It is rejected only when neither exists. A `location` sent on a `shop` job is ignored. If `name` is omitted it defaults to the joined names of the referenced items (e.g. the vehicle names). Jobs are always created `unpaid`. To record an invoice that was already collected, create the job and then record the money with `POST /v1/payments`, which settles the invoice and derives the payment status. When importing history, set `completedAt` to the original completion date along with `status: completed` so the job reports in the right period. The earnings and profit reports only count completed jobs, so `completedAt` without that status is rejected rather than silently leaving the revenue out of every figure. Likewise `canceledAt` requires `status: canceled` in the same request. New jobs pick up the account's default reminders, but the immediate 'job scheduled' confirmation message is suppressed by default so imports can't mass-message customers — pass `deployScheduledMessage: true` to send it (future-dated jobs only, and only when the account's scheduled-message auto-deploy preference is on).

industry.description: The industry the job belongs to.
industry.title: Industry

itemIds.description: The items/vehicles the job is for.
itemIds.title: Itemids

name.description: Defaults to the joined item names if omitted.
name.title: Name

location.description: Where the work is performed. Applies to `field` jobs; ignored on `shop` jobs. Defaults to the customer's location when omitted, so a field job is rejected only if neither is present. `formattedAddress`, `geoPoint` and `timeZone` are derived from the address server-side.

completedAt.description: Unix ms the work was finished. Set this when importing history: it is the date the earnings, profit, and product/service reports bucket a job on. Requires `status: completed` in the same request, since those reports only count completed jobs.
completedAt.title: Completedat

canceledAt.description: Unix ms the job was canceled. Set this when importing history so the canceled jobs list sorts on the original cancellation date. Requires `status: canceled` in the same request.
canceledAt.title: Canceledat

color.description: Calendar color for the job. `name` is the label shown for the color. Send `null` to clear it.

autoTax.title: Autotax

deployScheduledMessage.description: Set true to send the customer the immediate 'job scheduled' confirmation message for this job; by default API-created jobs suppress it, so imports can't mass-message customers. The job's other reminders (appointment reminders, follow-ups) deploy normally either way. Even when true, the confirmation only sends when the account's scheduled-message auto-deploy preference is on and the job's `start` is in the future.
deployScheduledMessage.title: Deployscheduledmessage

UrableUpdateJobConfig.description: Update a job. Requires scope `jobs:write`. Only supplied fields are changed. If `lineItems` is supplied the invoice is recomputed; otherwise the existing invoice is preserved. Because a job's line items are grouped under the item they are for, `itemIds` and `lineItems` move together: send the line items alongside any change to `itemIds` (they are rebuilt against the new set, and items dropped from the job lose their line items). Payment status is derived from the invoice and cannot be set here; record money with `POST /v1/payments`. A supplied `location` replaces the job's address outright (the derived `formattedAddress`, `geoPoint` and `timeZone` are all recomputed). On a job that is or becomes `field` and has no location yet, the customer's is copied onto it; the request is rejected only when neither exists. Changing `type` to `shop` clears the job's location.

industry.description: The industry the job belongs to.
industry.title: Industry

itemIds.description: The items/vehicles the job is for. Replaces the job's items, so `lineItems` must be sent with it.
itemIds.title: Itemids

location.description: Where the work is performed. Replaces the job's address outright, recomputing `formattedAddress`, `geoPoint` and `timeZone`. Ignored on `shop` jobs, and cleared when `type` changes to `shop`.

completedAt.description: Unix ms the work was finished. Set this when importing history: it is the date the earnings, profit, and product/service reports bucket a job on. Requires the job to end up `completed`, either by sending `status: completed` here or because it already is.
completedAt.title: Completedat

canceledAt.description: Unix ms the job was canceled. Requires the job to end up `canceled`, either by sending `status: canceled` here or because it already is.
canceledAt.title: Canceledat
